Before we lock in a kickoff, can you confirm:

- What you need from our side (example payloads, schema, tech lead).
- Any common pitfalls around structured output JSON schemas you advise avoiding.

I've looped in our technical mailbox (tech@healx.health) — they can share sample payloads. Looking to set a kickoff next week (Oct 4–6).

Appreciate it,

Hi Liam — great to hear you're ready to move forward. Happy to coordinate kickoff next week; Oct 5 (Tue) or Oct 6 (Wed) both look good on our side.

Quick answers up front:
- Typical activation cadence: a short pre-kickoff sync, 90-min technical kickoff (SRE/SW + SAs), 2–3 dev pairing sessions focused on streaming + tool-call integration, and an acceptance/QA review. I can share a one-page cadence doc.
- We need: sample JSON payloads, a list of the functions you expect us to call (name + input/output), and the tech lead(s) who will be on the call.
- Pitfalls: ambiguous schema fields, inconsistent enums across producers, and unbounded arrays that prevent streaming chunking. We'll validate schema against our structured-output linter.

Diego will propose a technical runbook and Monica will own the activation plan. Sending a proposed agenda in a follow-up.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — Diego from Solutions here. Attaching a compact technical plan and checklist for the streaming + function-calling work (see attachment stubs below). High-level items I want to cover during the kickoff:

- Goals (day 0 primer):
  * End-to-end streaming generation with client-side partial rendering
  * 2 function calls (createTicket, enrichPatient) wired to your webhook
  * Structured JSON v1 validation on every turn

- Pre-kickoff deliverables (from HealX):
  * sample_payload.json (representative examples for short and long sequences)
  * function spec: name + required params + expected outputs (JSON schema or OpenAPI snippet)
  * network egress/wildcard IPs or VPC peering constraints for private deployments

- Tech notes / constraints:
  * Streaming: use chunk-safe delimiters (we recommend newline-prefixed JSON chunks) and include incremental partial states for UI rendering.
  * Tool calling: prefer idempotent function designs; include a correlation_id on every call so retries are safe.
  * Structured outputs: we will run your schema through our linter and flag any unbounded union types.
  * Performance: for sub-1500 token responses we rely on batching size=16 for predictable latency; call out if you expect higher concurrency.

Attachments (stubs): schema_v1.json (application/json), implementation_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

Proposed 45/90 minute technical kickoff agenda (I can draft a Google Doc after we pick a slot). Let me know the tech lead and sample files and I'll pre-validate the schema before the call.

- Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Thanks Diego — attaching a quick sample payload and a short function list. See inline answers below.

Sample payload: attached as sample_payload.json (contains two event types: encounter.summary and encounter.update).

Function list (we want to start with two):
- createTicket
  * inputs: patient_id (string), summary (string), priority (enum)
  * outputs: ticket_id (string), status (enum)
- enrichPatient
  * inputs: patient_id (string), data_refs (array<string>)
  * outputs: enrichment_status (enum), new_fields (object)

Notes from our tech team:
- We prefer function calls to be synchronous with an acknowledgement payload (so the UI can show immediate success).
- For streaming, we will render partial summaries; can Redwood emit interim structured JSON objects that the client can parse?

Available for kickoff: Oct 6 afternoon (US Pacific). Thanks — sending sample payload now.

Liam

Subject: Quick implementation note: tokenization & fallback variants

Quick note before the kickoff:
- For structured streaming we recommend a max stable chunk payload of ~1200 tokens to keep incremental latency predictable; if your expected messages exceed that frequently, call that out so we can set batching and KV-cache sizing appropriately.
- For function calls that must be synchronous, we suggest a paired fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) for degraded capacity to preserve availability.
- We'll prepare a short internal run showing the createTicket -> webhook acknowledgement flow; if the webhook can respond within 2s we can keep the user flow synchronous.

Happy to jump on the kickoff; Diego/Naomi/Monica — please add me to the calendar invite.

Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
